t: You're looking at the Piranesi Vase, also called the Boyd Vase, a colossal marble calyx krater from ancient Rome. It stands on three legs and a triangular base, with a relief running around its sides, and it is about two and a half metres tall, at 2.71 metres. It was reconstructed by Giovanni Battista Piranesi from ancient fragments. Piranesi was a classical archaeologist, architect and artist, famous for his etchings of Rome and of imagined, atmospheric prisons. So the vase is partly ancient, and partly his own creation.
